subject: Meteorology
title: The Weather Diary Tradition
description: One-minute skill: The Weather Diary Tradition.

hook.text: Before instruments existed, dedicated observers kept daily weather diaries—some spanning decades of sky descriptions.

buildup.text: William Merle in 14th-century England kept one of the earliest known weather journals—seven years of daily notes.

discovery.text: These diaries were qualitative—describing wind, clouds, rain, and temperature in words rather than numbers.

twist.text: Thomas Jefferson kept meticulous weather records—he was recording temperatures on the day he signed the Declaration.

climax.text: Historical weather diaries are now invaluable for climate research—filling gaps before instrument records began.

punchline.text: Pen, paper, and patience—the first weather data was handwritten.

quiz.question: Why are historical weather diaries valuable today?
options: They fill gaps in climate data before instruments existed
